rationale: Ground truth has no substantive reviewer concerns (just LGTM/approve), so both trivially achieve full recall. X gives a tight, well-evidenced verification of the diff's three claims with specific file:line citations and correctly recommends approval, but offers only one soft, low-confidence comment — thin on actionable follow-up. Y verifies the same core claims with comparable rigor and additionally surfaces a genuinely useful, grounded issue outside the diff (the sibling gradio README still documents the buggy nested extra_body form, which could re-confuse users right after this fix) plus a concrete index-collision nit on the new two-choices behavior, both with specific file:line evidence and suggested edits — more actionable, though the unit-test ask stretches scope for a docs-only PR. Overall Y edges out on actionability and thoroughness without sacrificing grounding.
